title: Redwood Renewal & Expansion Check-in - NovaHealth
summary: Check-in to discuss upcoming renewal, request for additional GPU capacity and APAC region coverage; customer evaluating committed capacity vs burst pricing. Agreed next steps: size Dedicated pool, send updated quote, provide compliance docs and run a benchmark in APAC region.
next_steps: Redwood: send updated renewal quote with Dedicated capacity options and pricing by 2025-03-14
Redwood: schedule Dedicated sizing workshop with Maya and Luis for next week
Redwood: share SOC2 + ISO docs, DPA, and KMS integration notes
NovaHealth: confirm target throughput (req/s and avg seq length) and preferred APAC region by 2025-03-13
All: agree on pilot timeline for APAC benchmark by end of March
transcript:
Meeting header:
Date: 2025-03-10
Start: 15:30 PT
Duration: ~55 minutes
Attendees: Alex Moreno (Redwood AE), Priya Desai (Redwood SE), Omar Li (Redwood CSM), Sam Patel (CTO - NovaHealth), Maya Chen (Head of ML Ops), Jordan Reeves (Procurement), Luis Torres (SRE)

[00:00] Alex: Hey everyone, thanks for carving out time. This is our renewal and expansion check-in for NovaHealth, I'm Alex from Redwood, with Priya our solutions engineer and Omar our CSM. How's everyone doing?
[00:12] Sam: Good, thanks. Busy but excited to get this locked down.
[00:15] Maya: Yeah, thanks for setting this up. We have a few items: capacity needs, APAC coverage, and contract questions.
[00:23] Alex: Perfect, that's exactly what we wanted to cover. Quick agenda: renewal timing and options, Dedicated capacity sizing and pricing, regions / latency impact, security/compliance ask, and then next steps.
[00:35] Priya: I'll jump into the workload numbers quickly to ground the sizing convo. Maya, you shared some telemetry last week — 300 rps peak for the chat endpoint and an average sequence length around 320 tokens? Is that still right?
[00:48] Maya: That's right, peaks around 300, steady-state 120 rps. But keep in mind we have bursty traffic during mornings. Sequence length average is 320 historically but for a new triage flow it can go up to 700.
[01:02] Priya: Got it. That heavier tail is important for KV cache and batching decisions. For Dedicated, we typically recommend a small warm pool for the 700 sequence tails to avoid cold start latency.
[01:16] Speaker 2: (inaudible)
[01:20] Alex: On renewal terms, Jordan from procurement — any constraints on committing to a 12 vs 24 month reserved capacity deal?
[01:28] Jordan: We're generally fine with a 12 month commit but need options. Our procurement team prefers annual but wants a clear right-sizing clause if utilization deviates more than 30% after the first quarter. Also need clarity on break clauses and termination for convenience.
[01:44] Luis: And for APAC, we need a region in Singapore or Sydney with <120ms p95 to our client endpoints in APAC. Latency's a big metric for us.
[01:54] Priya: We can run a Dedicated pool in ap-southeast-1; we've validated p95 ~90-110ms in similar setups but we'll need to run your real workload. For the exact p95 we'll need a benchmark with your token distribution.
[02:11] Sam: Pricing question: committed vs on-demand — how aggressive can we get for committed pricing for baseline throughput?
[02:18] Alex: We can provide tiered discounts based on committed GPU-hours or vGPU equivalents. For example, a 12 month reserved pool at 60% utilization helps us offer a meaningful discount vs hosted on-demand. We can show numbers in the quote.
[02:30] Maya: One of our concerns is quality regression if you route to smaller quantized variants as a fallback to save cost. We need guarantees or automatic rollback if evals fail.
[02:40] Priya: Totally. We have rollout policies and quality monitors tied to prompt sets. We can configure auto-rollback on any regression above a defined threshold. We'll also attach a baseline eval for your triage flow.
[02:52] Sam: Great. Also security — SOC 2, SSO, KMS, audit logs, DPA — standard asks. We need the SOC 2 cert and details on customer-managed keys.
[03:02] Alex: We'll share SOC 2 Type II and ISO docs. Regarding KMS, we support customer-managed keys in Dedicated and Private deployments; for hosted we'll propose BYOK integration patterns and HSM-backed KMS notes.
[03:15] Jordan: Can you include indemnity language and data residency notes in the updated quote? Also, any changes to data retention for debug logs?
[03:23] Omar: We can set retention controls per project and provide exportable audit logs. We'll include the DPA and data retention options in the package.
[03:33] [05:00] Priya: Back to capacity sizing — if we design for 300 pk rps with burst to 700 for short windows, we recommend a Dedicated pool equivalent to 10 A100-class GPUs with scaled burst licensing for an extra 3 GPUs during peak. That ratio depends on model (we used a 70B dense for these estimates).
[05:18] Maya: 10 A100s seems reasonable. Can you provide a lower-cost option with quantized 4-bit weights for lower-priority routes?
[05:26] Priya: Yes, we can map lower-priority routes to a quantized variant — same model family but 4-bit — and ensure routing policies avoid quality-sensitive prompts. We'll also expose per-route SLOs so you can cap cost/latency tradeoffs.
[05:40] Sam: Important to us is graceful degradation: if Dedicated is constrained, automatic fallback to hosted with throttles is fine as long as we get predictable latency.
[05:50] Alex: Agreed. We'll configure smart routing: primary Dedicated, fallback to hosted API (same family of model variants) with controlled burst budgets.
[05:58] [10:12] Luis: On the APAC benchmark, we want Redwood to run a 24-hour run with our traffic replay of morning peak. We'll need credentials for a test environment and a small dataset for eval.
[10:23] Priya: We'll coordinate offline - please send the replay artifacts and we'll spin up an APAC Dedicated staging pool for the run. This will also surface any model variant quality diffs.
[10:34] Jordan: Timeline question — when do you need a signed commitment to hit May 1 start?
[10:39] Alex: For provisioning Dedicated in APAC and meeting SLAs, we need a signed order form by 2025-04-01 to be safe; earlier gives us more flexibility. We'll include provisioning lead times in the quote.
[10:50] Maya: Can we get a short pilot/POC window with reduced commitment to validate APAC latency and cost? Maybe a 30-day pilot before full commit.
[10:59] Alex: Yes, we can structure a pilot as a time-limited reserved pool with conversion credits if you convert to a full 12 month commit. We'll include that option.
[11:08] [20:05] Sam: A few technical details: cross-region KV cache warming, prefix caching and whether session affinity is required. We don't want cold starts on hospital triage flows.
[20:15] Priya: We recommend sticky sessions for flows that benefit from KV cache, or a shared KV cache across tail nodes; depends on your consistency needs. There is slight complexity for cross-region replication but it's doable. We might see additional cost for cross-region KV sync.
[20:32] Maya: How does the billing granularly show token-level cost vs infra amortization? We need visibility to tie to product metrics.
[20:39] Omar: Redwood Console has token-level and model-level cost breakdowns. For Dedicated we provide amortized infra cost per request and a per-token runtime breakdown in the billing export. We'll attach a sample billing export.
[20:54] Jordan: One more from legal — can you confirm data deletion timelines on contract termination? Some of our regulators require 90 days.
[21:02] Alex: We'll confirm but standard is 30 days; for an enterprise SLA we can negotiate 90 days and include it in the SOW.
[21:10] [30:00] Priya: Recap of items I captured: 1) Dedicated sizing workshop, 2) APAC benchmark run, 3) Shared eval set for auto-rollback, 4) updated quote with pilot option, 5) compliance docs to procurement. Anything missing?
[30:20] Maya: Also include clear right-sizing clause and conversion credits for pilot.
[30:26] Jordan: Add termination notice and data residency language.
[30:31] Alex: We'll include all of that.
[30:35] Sam: Sounds good. On the metrics side, if we can get a p95 <120ms for APAC on the benchmark, we're comfortable moving forward.
[30:44] Priya: We'll prioritize that during the benchmark and report back.
[30:50] [40:00] Omar: I'll follow up in CRM with a link to the quote and attach the SOC2/ISO artifacts. Alex will own the quote. Priya will own the Dedicated sizing workshop and the benchmark run.
[40:12] Alex: Timeline again: we'll aim to send quote by Friday 2025-03-14, schedule the sizing workshop for week of 2025-03-17, and run the APAC benchmark by end of March. Jordan — is that timeline OK for procurement reviews?
[40:28] Jordan: Yes, that works. We may need another legal touchpoint but procurement can review the initial docs and escalate.
[40:35] Sam: One more small ask — can you include examples of per-route SLO configuration and a mock cost-savings dashboard?
[40:43] Omar: We'll include the sample dashboard and a recommended per-route SLO table.
[40:49] [52:00] Alex: Great, thanks everyone. Quick recap in plain language: Redwood to send updated renewal quote with Dedicated/APAC options and pilot conversion credits by 2025-03-14; Redwood to schedule sizing workshop and run APAC benchmark with NovaHealth artifacts; Redwood to provide compliance artifacts; NovaHealth to confirm region and throughput by 2025-03-13. We'll reconvene after the benchmark to finalize order form.
[52:25] Maya: Awesome, thanks.
[52:28] Jordan: Thanks all.
[52:30] Alex: Thanks, talk soon.

End of transcript.
